screenplay.text:
MARKET DAY

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

               EXT. CITY MARKET - DAWN

               Stalls go up under striped awnings. Crates of mangoes,
               pyramids of tomatoes, sacks of mealie meal stacked like
               sandbags.

               AUNTIE PRECIOUS (60s), floral headscarf, reading glasses on
               a beaded chain, arranges tins of spice in a perfect fan.
               Every label faces forward.

               Across the aisle, a new stall. YUSUF (20s), apron over a
               football shirt, hangs a hand-painted sign: CHEAPEST SPICE IN
               TOWN.

               Auntie Precious lowers her glasses and reads it.

                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                         Cheapest. Hm. Cheap is not a
                         flavour.

                                     YUSUF
                         Good morning to you too, Auntie.

               INT. MARKET HALL - DAY

               The hall is loud and full. Shoppers push trolleys between
               the stalls. A pigeon walks along a rafter.

               A WOMAN WITH A PRAM stops between the two stalls. She looks
               left. She looks right.

                                     YUSUF
                         Peri-peri, sister! Half the price
                         of over there!

                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                               (not looking up)
                         And half the taste.

               The woman buys from Auntie Precious. Yusuf throws his hands
               up.

               INT. MARKET HALL - LATER

               Yusuf sits on an upturned crate eating a samoosa. Auntie
               Precious weighs out turmeric on a brass SCALE.

               A small boy, KAMO (7), tugs at her skirt.

                                     KAMO
                         Gogo, he has more customers than
                         you.








                                                                       2.


                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                         He has more noise than me. That is
                         a different thing.

               INT. MARKET HALL - AFTERNOON

               A roof gutter overflows. Water pours straight down onto
               Yusuf's stall. His spice tins float in a spreading yellow
               puddle.

                                     YUSUF
                         No! No, no, no!

               He grabs at tins with both hands. The CHEAPEST SPICE sign
               peels off and slides into the water.

               Auntie Precious watches over her glasses. Then she stands,
               picks up an empty crate and marches across the aisle.

                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                         Stop grabbing. Lift. Crates under,
                         tins on top. Kamo! Newspaper!

               Kamo runs with an armful of old newspaper. The three of them
               build a dry tower of crates.

                                     YUSUF
                         Why are you helping me?

                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                         Because if your peri-peri gets wet
                         it will taste even worse.

               EXT. CITY MARKET - DUSK

               The awnings come down. The puddle shines orange in the last
               of the sun.

               Yusuf repaints his sign on a flattened box. Auntie Precious
               reads it over his shoulder.

               The new sign says: SECOND BEST SPICE IN TOWN.

                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                               (smiling)
                         Now that is honest advertising.

                                     YUSUF
                         Tomorrow I will be first.

                                     AUNTIE PRECIOUS
                         Tomorrow you will be early. Start
                         there.









                                                                       3.


               She hands him one of her own tins of spice and walks away
               into the dusk with Kamo.

                                                            FADE OUT.

shots.source:
Stalls go up under striped awnings. Crates of mangoes, pyramids of tomatoes, sacks of mealie meal stacked like sandbags.
AUNTIE PRECIOUS (60s), floral headscarf, reading glasses on a beaded chain, arranges tins of spice in a perfect fan. Every label faces forward.
Across the aisle, a new stall. YUSUF (20s), apron over a football shirt, hangs a hand-painted sign: CHEAPEST SPICE IN TOWN.
shots.rationale: Establishes the dawn market layout and positions both vendors within their stalls.

shots.source:
Auntie Precious lowers her glasses and reads it.
Cheapest. Hm. Cheap is not a flavour.
shots.rationale: Tight on Auntie's face as she evaluates the price claim, emphasizing her skepticism.

shots.source: Good morning to you too, Auntie.
shots.rationale: Captures Yusuf's relaxed greeting after the exchange, framing him in the stall he set up.

shots.source:
The hall is loud and full. Shoppers push trolleys between the stalls. A pigeon walks along a rafter.
A WOMAN WITH A PRAM stops between the two stalls. She looks left. She looks right.
shots.rationale: Establishes the chaotic market atmosphere and positions all characters before the interaction begins.

shots.source:
Peri-peri, sister! Half the price of over there!
And half the taste.
shots.rationale: Frames the price negotiation between the two vendors at medium distance.

shots.source: The woman buys from Auntie Precious. Yusuf throws his hands up.
shots.rationale: Tightens on the woman's reaction as she makes the purchase decision.

shots.source:
Yusuf sits on an upturned crate eating a samoosa. Auntie Precious weighs out turmeric on a brass SCALE.
A small boy, KAMO (7), tugs at her skirt.
shots.rationale: Establishes the shared space and the scale as KAMO interrupts.

shots.source: Gogo, he has more customers than you.
shots.rationale: Tightens on KAMO's accusatory line to heighten the tension.

shots.source: He has more noise than me. That is a different thing.
shots.rationale: Allows AUNTIE PRECIOUS to deliver the rebuttal while keeping the scale in frame.

shots.source:
A roof gutter overflows. Water pours straight down onto Yusuf's stall. His spice tins float in a spreading yellow puddle.
No! No, no, no!
shots.rationale: Establishes the flooding stall and Yusuf's panic in a single view.

shots.source:
He grabs at tins with both hands. The CHEAPEST SPICE sign peels off and slides into the water.
Auntie Precious watches over her glasses. Then she stands, picks up an empty crate and marches across the aisle.
shots.rationale: Captures Yusuf's frantic grabbing and Auntie's corrective stance.

Kamo runs with an armful of old newspaper. The three of them build a dry tower of crates.
shots.rationale: Frames the collaborative tower-building action with all participants.

Because if your peri-peri gets wet it will taste even worse.
shots.rationale: Tightens on the exchange about the wet peri-peri flavor.

shots.rationale: Establishes the shared workspace as the awnings lower and the sun catches the puddle.

shots.source:

shots.rationale: Frames the new sign and Auntie's reaction, keeping both faces visible for the exchange.

shots.source:

shots.rationale: Captures the banter about timing and ambition as the light fades.

shots.rationale: A close moment on Auntie accepting the tin and stepping into dusk with Kamo.
